reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it primarily teaches viewers how to transfer Litecoin from Coinbase to Binance, including selecting the correct deposit address, scanning a QR code, and waiting for confirmation. It also promotes cryptocurrency platform referral links and describes a $10 signup-related Bitcoin incentive, but the evidence does not establish a deceptive solicitation or a false guaranteed financial outcome. The creator's role is instructional with some affiliate-style promotion.

citations.quote: How to transfer Litecoin or Bitcoin from Coinbase to Binance
I'm going to show you guys how to transfer like one from Coinbase to Binance.
it's very important that you make sure that you're sending it to the correct location.
I'm going to put my pin in. And then bam. As you can see I just sent the Litecoin.
Once you buy or sell $100 of digital currency or more will get $10 of free bitcoin.

opening.argument: The promotional material makes the reward conditional on a concrete financial action: the description says viewers who buy or sell at least $100 of digital currency will get $10 in Bitcoin, and provides a Coinbase join link. The speaker reinforces that offer by saying both parties get Bitcoin when the viewer deposits $100, then offers to send a link if the viewer texts a phone number. This is not merely discussion of a possible reward; it connects a crypto deposit and contact with the creator to acquiring the promised asset. That action-for-reward pitch warrants treating the video as a solicitation whose terms and fulfillment are not established by the presentation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The transfer walkthrough does not resolve the separate acquisition pitch. Showing a deposit address, scanning a QR code, and waiting for confirmation establishes that a transfer is demonstrated; it does not establish the terms or fulfillment of the advertised Bitcoin reward. The description expressly ties that reward to buying or selling $100, and the speaker ties it to a deposit and texting for a link. Calling the overall presentation instructional leaves that concrete solicitation unaddressed.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A conditional referral incentive is not, by itself, evidence that the reward is false or that the transfer is a scam. The video demonstrates a Litecoin transfer between exchange interfaces, including its confirmation, while the description states a specific threshold and links to Coinbase. The speaker's offer to send a referral link likewise does not show that anyone was misled or that the promised Bitcoin was withheld. The argument identifies a promotion, but does not establish deception.

you my link Yeah, you and I would get $10 dollars in free bitcoin

opening.argument: The pitch layers several easy-to-understand incentives around crypto participation: a promised $10 in Bitcoin after a $100 transaction, a recommended platform advertised as having zero fees, and an Uber signup offer described as a "$50 - $1250 GUARANTEE or Bonus." The description supplies destinations and referral details alongside these claims, while the speaker also solicits a phone number to send a Coinbase link. These are real promotional cues, not proof that any particular claim is false. But their combination encourages viewers to act on unusually attractive financial language without the video establishing the relevant conditions, limits, or whether the rewards will be received. That gap makes the reward solicitation a substantial scam concern.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The fact that the video also teaches transfers does not neutralize the promotional context around that instruction. The description puts a Bitcoin reward, an external investment-platform recommendation, and a large variable signup claim in the same promotional space. The demonstration can make exchange participation feel routine, but it cannot establish that the associated incentives are unconditional or that viewers will receive them. The argument is about the combined solicitation and missing terms, not a claim that the transfer itself failed.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotional language and referral links are visible, but they do not show that the listed incentives are deceptive. The Bitcoin offer gives a stated $100 threshold, and the video does not claim guaranteed trading profits; it explains that viewers can transfer Litecoin and may trade it for other assets. Nor does the unrelated Uber offer establish that the crypto demonstration is fraudulent. The evidence supports mixed instructional and promotional content, not a demonstrated false reward.

opening.argument: The tutorial framing also serves a promotional function: the speaker recommends Binance, says he will leave a signup link, emphasizes its low fees and access to many tokens, and describes Coinbase as a gateway for buying crypto. The walkthrough then shows the operational steps for moving Litecoin into Binance, while the description adds a Bitcoin reward linked to a $100 transaction and a referral link. This is more than abstract education; it guides viewers toward exchange participation and pairs that pathway with an asset incentive. The video never establishes that the reward's terms are complete or that it will be delivered, so the instructional format should not obscure the actionable promotional pitch.

citations.quote: I will leave a link in the description below, you can sign up for Binance.
the fees on Binance are so much cheaper
your Coinbase account can be like your gateway account to cryptocurrencies.
Once you buy or sell $100 of digital currency or more will get $10 of free bitcoin.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's own account recognizes affiliate-style promotion, but understates how the video turns that promotion into an actionable route: it recommends an exchange, demonstrates sending Litecoin to it, and links a Bitcoin reward to a qualifying transaction. A working tutorial can increase confidence in the destination without verifying the referral offer's conditions or delivery. The point is not that every exchange demonstration is fraudulent; it is that the tutorial frame does not answer the reward-based solicitation embedded in this one.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The visible substance remains an operational demonstration: the speaker explains how to select a Litecoin deposit destination, send Litecoin, and wait for it to arrive. Recommending an exchange and disclosing referral links may make the video promotional, but neither establishes a false promise. The reward is described with a transaction threshold; the supplied evidence does not show that it was unavailable, misrepresented, or withheld. Promotion is not enough to turn the demonstrated transfer into a scam.
